test_title: PYST 41: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 21 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following is/are correct regarding the agricultural sector post the reform period of 1991?

1. Quantitative restrictions on imports of agricultural products to India were fully removed from April 2001.

2. There was a huge increase in the import duties on agricultural products to India after 1991.

3. Due to the export-oriented policy after 1991, there was a shift from production for the domestic market towards production for the export market, with more focus on cash crops than food grains.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Post the **1991 economic reforms in India**, the agricultural sector underwent significant changes, particularly with the introduction of trade liberalization policies.
 
• **Quantitative restrictions** on imports of agricultural products were fully removed in **April 2001**, marking a major step toward integrating Indian agriculture into the global economy.
 
• India adopted an **export-oriented policy**, emphasizing production for international markets. This led to a shift from traditional food grain cultivation to the cultivation of **cash crops** such as cotton, sugarcane, and spices.
 
• The removal of quantitative restrictions and export-focused policies were aligned with the goals of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, to which India is a signatory.
 
• This shift had significant implications for food security and rural livelihoods, as the focus on cash crops sometimes came at the expense of food grain production for the domestic market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 2: Increase in import duties**__

 __
 
• Contrary to the claim in Option 2, import duties on agricultural products were not significantly increased after 1991. Instead, the focus was on **reducing trade barriers** to facilitate globalization and trade liberalization.
 
• India adhered to WTO norms that emphasized **lower tariffs and reduced trade barriers** for agricultural commodities.
 
 
 
• **Quantitative restrictions (Option 1)**__
 __
 
• The removal of **quantitative restrictions** was a significant policy change post-1991, and it allowed India to import agricultural products more freely.
 
• This policy aimed to integrate Indian agriculture with global markets, promoting competition and accessibility to diverse agricultural goods.
 
 
 
• **Export-oriented policy (Option 3)**__
 
 
• India's post-1991 export-oriented policy led to an increased focus on **cash crop production**, which was economically lucrative in international markets.
 
• Examples of cash crops include **tea, coffee, spices, cotton, and tobacco**, which gained prominence over traditional food grains.
 
• This policy was aimed at earning foreign exchange and enhancing India's agricultural trade competitiveness globally.
